relations.evidence: To try the examples in this section, set the query context to the `inventory` scope in the travel sample dataset. For more information, see [Query Context](../n1ql-intro/queriesandresults.md#query-context).

notable_absence.finding: No Prerequisites/RBAC section at all, unlike LET, INFER, JOIN, and INSERT in this same batch. LIMIT is a modifier clause used inside SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE rather than a standalone statement, so it inherits whatever privilege the enclosing statement requires instead of declaring its own - the credential-type/privilege model attaches at the statement level, not to every clause nested within one.

cross_product_finding: RECURRENCE of the known anomaly logged in docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json: 'Starting from version 4.5, the LIMIT clause in INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements is no longer a hint. It indicates that the actual number of mutations will be less than or equal to the specified LIMIT.' Capella has no discrete version numbers, yet this page cites a literal (implicitly Couchbase Server) version number.
